TLDR News.title: GLM-5.2 (6 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: Z.ai launched GLM-5.2 with a 1 million-token context window, new reasoning controls, and support for long-horizon coding tasks across entire codebases. The company made the model available immediately to Coding Plan users and plans to release API access, chatbot support, technical details, and MIT-licensed open weights the following week. Z.ai positions GLM-5.2 as a coding-first upgrade focused on agentic software engineering, though it did not publish benchmark results at launch.

TLDR News.title: Android 17 Expands AI Agent Integration (8 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: Android 17 introduced new AI-focused capabilities centered on AppFunctions and Android MCP, enabling apps to expose orchestratable tools that on-device agents can discover and execute. Google positioned the release as part of a broader shift toward an “intelligence system” with deeper AI integration across the platform.

TLDR News.title: Qwen's Embodied World Modeling (28 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: Qwen-RobotWorld is a language-conditioned video world model that uses natural language as a unified action interface across robotics, navigation, driving, and other embodied domains.

TLDR News.title: Cursor Origin (1 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: Cursor Origin is an attempt at an agent-native GitHub competitor. The Git-compatible forge is built around the assumption that lots of AI agents will be cloning, branching, committing, rebasing, reviewing, and fixing failures in parallel. Cursor is trying to own the whole AI software factory. GitHub was built for human-scale development, but Origin was built for agent-scale.

TLDR News.title: OpenAI released CDP support for browser use on Codex (2 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: OpenAI's Codex now supports Chrome DevTools Protocol, enabling live browser access to profile JavaScript performance and modify websites in real time. This early-stage feature, available via opt-in settings but excluded from the EEA, UK, and Switzerland, faces performance issues and requires careful prompting. Recent OpenAI moves, such as acquiring Ona, aim to create persistent cloud environments, highlighting a push toward an AI-driven web.

TLDR News.title: Fastest, Largest, Strongest: NVIDIA Blackwell Sweeps MLPerf Training 6.0 (6 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: NVIDIA's Blackwell platform dominated MLPerf Training 6.0 benchmarks, achieving the fastest training times and the largest-scale training with 8,192 GPUs. Blackwell's NVLink and NVFP4 innovations enhance performance by efficiently routing MoE models and enabling rapid, large-scale training. Reliability features like the Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability Engine and NVIDIA Resiliency Extension ensure minimal downtime and faster recovery in large-scale AI environments.

TLDR News.title: Anthropic “pauses” token-based billing for its Claude Agent SDK (4 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: Anthropic has paused the pricing changes it announced last month, just before they were set to take effect. The change would have treated Claude Agent SDK usage separately from standard Claude usage. Outside SDK usage will now be billed at Anthropic's prevailing API rates. Anthropic is working to update its plans to better support how users build with Claude subscriptions.

TLDR News.title: Qualcomm wants to be the chip inside whatever replaces your smartphone, and it just announced two products toward that end (4 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: Qualcomm is working on over 40 different AI wearable devices. It has announced a platform called Snapdragon Reality Elite for mixed-reality glass and the Scalable Turnkey AI-Ready toolkit, a combination of hardware models and a software stack for AI devices. The company is aiming to position itself as the foundational silicon layer for whatever is coming after the smartphone. It is experimenting with a range of potential form factors that can work with AI technologies.

TLDR News.title: Never waste a token (15 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: Crashes waste tokens when the provider connection lives inside the thing that crashed, so move it out.

TLDR News.title: OpenAI prepares major ChatGPT voice upgrade with GPT-Bidi-1 (2 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: GPT-Bidi-1 is a bidirectional audio model for ChatGPT's voice mode designed to listen and speak at once, absorb interruptions, and adjust mid-sentence.

TLDR News.title: Why Weibo's tiny VibeThinker-3B has the AI world arguing over benchmarks again (15 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: The 3B parameter model put up coding benchmark scores in the same league as Claude Opus 4.5.

TLDR News.title: Microsoft Tests Phi Silica for Windows AI on Nvidia GPUs (6 minute read)
TLDR News.excerpt: Microsoft's Phi Silica small language models are explicitly engineered to run locally on the Neural Processing Units of Windows Copilot+ PCs.
